captions.instagram:
On an F-1 or J-1 visa with no U.S. income? There's still one IRS form for you.

✔️ Form 8843 explains why your days as a student don't count toward U.S. tax residency.
✔️ It's needed even with no income, and each F-2 or J-2 family member files their own.
✔️ No 2026 income? Mail it by itself by June 15, 2027.
✔️ Had wages or a taxable scholarship? Attach it to Form 1040-NR instead.

This is tax information only, not immigration advice. We prepare Form 8843 on its own ($25), or with your Form 1040-NR in our student package with a tax-treaty check ($99 federal, $129 with one state return). Federal plus NJ and NY returns. Book a call to start. Not available for CA, CT, MD or OR state returns.

sources.fact: Even if the student or scholar had no income, they still must file Form 8843 by the 15th day of the 6th month (June 15); one for each family member in F-2 or J-2 status (Pub 4011 Rev. 10-2026, read 2026-10-24)
Form 8843: attach to Form 1040-NR if filing one; if no return is required, mail Form 8843 by itself (2025 form instructions; 2026 form not yet issued, read 2026-10-24)
Students on F, J, M or Q visas who substantially comply are exempt individuals; their days don't count for the substantial presence test (read 2026-10-24)
F/J/M/Q students must file Form 1040-NR only if they have taxable income such as wages or scholarship grants; no wages subject to withholding -> 15th day of 6th month (read 2026-10-24)
